methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $5M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.5x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Gallox Semiconductors is a Seed-stage chip design company founded by Jon McCandless and Debdeep Jena that has raised $5M+. The Chips & Semiconductors sector contains 11 total comparables (3 public, 8 private), including peers such as Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems, though none provide sufficient data density for direct peer-median valuation at this stage.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable triangulation method here. Using the $5M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a standard 2.5x Seed-to-next-stage multiplier yields an implied valuation of $12M. This reflects typical dilution and value-creation patterns in semiconductor company financing progression.

The public comparables universe—ALAB, NVDA, and AMD trading at a sector-median P/S of 21.5x—cannot be directly applied without Gallox's revenue, which private companies rarely disclose. Peer-median methods failed due to insufficient same- and adjacent-stage datapoints within the narrow Chips & Semiconductors cohort. The valuation analysis therefore supports a range of $11M to $14M, centered on $12M. Key uncertainties include the absence of financial performance metrics, revenue trajectory, and technical validation milestones that would typically anchor valuations in capital-intensive semiconductor subsectors. Additional data on burn rate, product stage, and customer traction would materially refine this range.
